title: 60-day warning: Windows Server 2016 and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 lose free updates on 13 January 2027
summary: Microsoft's 60-day reminders (MC1551896, MC1551897, 13 November 2026): all Windows Server 2016 editions reach end of extended support on 13 January 2027, including the Server 2016 Essentials features such as Remote Web Access; Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 reaches end of mainstream support the same day. The January 2027 security update is the last one for both outside Extended Security Updates (ESU); for LTSC 2021, Microsoft says ESU is available for up to three years.
why: Server 2016 is still common on domain controllers, AD FS, RDS, file servers and line-of-business app hosts — exactly the tier-0/tier-1 systems where an unpatched month matters. LTSC 2021 often sits on kiosks, OT and medical devices that nobody re-images. Decide upgrade vs. ESU now; ESU procurement and key activation take longer than 60 days in most organisations.
todo: Inventory Server 2016 and LTSC 2021 everywhere: Intune/ConfigMgr for clients, Azure Resource Graph for Arc and Azure VMs, and AD computer objects for anything unmanaged.
Prioritise domain controllers, AD CS, AD FS and internet-facing RDS on Server 2016 for in-place upgrade or replacement before January.
For systems that cannot move in time, buy and activate ESU before 13 January 2027 and test that the January update installs (ESU activation is a separate step).
Retire any Server 2016 Essentials Remote Web Access exposure; it becomes unsupported functionality.
